html:
Tensile & compressive strain
The shaded solid cylinder is the undeformed rod of length L0. The violet dashed outline shows where the loaded end ends up: a dashed cap-cylinder outside the body in tension, a dashed ellipse inside it in compression.
Loading
ΔL = (1/Y)(F/A)L0 — linear in F; the radius (hence A) never changes.
Guided demo
Drag the figure to orbit — the end faces are true circles seen in perspective. Click the rod, an arrow, or the A marker for an explanation.

plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 12: Static Equilibrium and Elasticity
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two panels side by side, labeled (a) and (b) beneath them, each a shaded three-dimensional cylinder standing on end and representing the same rod under opposite loading. In panel (a) a thick red arrow labeled F points straight up from above the top face and a matching red arrow labeled F points straight down from below the bottom face; a dashed outline extends above the solid cylinder to mark the stretched portion, bracketed at the left as 'Delta L', with a longer bracket below it spanning the original length 'L0'. In panel (b) the two red arrows are reversed, pressing inward from above and below, a curly leader labels the top circular face 'A', and a bracket labeled 'Delta L' at the right runs from the top face down to a dashed ellipse drawn inside the cylinder where the end formerly sat, with 'L0' bracketed at the left. Both cylinders are drawn at identical width, so the whole comparison rests on whether the dashed reference outline lies outside or inside the solid body. The pairing defines the signed length change from the undeformed length L0 that enters tensile and compressive strain, with the cross-section held constant in the low-stress linear range.

elements: Vertical circular cylinder (rod) standing on end, shaded pale lavender with a light-to-dark vertical gradient and a thin blue-violet outline
Elliptical top face of the cylinder (seen slightly from above)
Elliptical bottom edge of the cylinder
Dashed elliptical/cylindrical reference outline extending ABOVE the solid body in tension mode (the stretched portion)
Dashed ellipse drawn INSIDE the cylinder in compression mode, marking where the top face originally sat
Thick red force arrow above the top face (points up in tension, down into the top face in compression), labeled vector F
Thick red force arrow below the bottom face (points down in tension, up into the bottom face in compression), labeled vector F
Left-hand vertical bracket with end ticks spanning the original length, labeled L0
Second vertical bracket labeled ΔL — placed at the left above the L0 bracket in tension mode, at the right between top face and dashed interior ellipse in compression mode
Curly leader line from the top face pointing to the label A (cross-sectional area), shown in compression mode
Panel caption text '(a)' for tension and '(b)' for compression beneath the cylinder
Vector labels F with bold arrow-over notation, italic labels L0, ΔL, A

interactions.label: Loading
interactions.teaches: The same rod under opposite loading: reversing the force arrows flips the sign of ΔL, so the dashed undeformed reference lies outside (stretched) or inside (shortened) the solid body.

interactions.label: Applied force F (relative)
interactions.teaches: ΔL grows in direct proportion to F while the radius stays fixed — the linear low-stress regime ΔL = (1/Y)(F/A)L0; passing through F = 0 returns the rod to its undeformed length L0.
interactions.note: Negative values are compression, positive tension; moving the slider across zero also switches the loadingMode panel labels/bracket placement.

interactions.teaches: The body is a solid cylinder of constant circular cross-section A, so the deformation is purely axial — the elliptical end faces are circles seen in perspective.

demo_steps.title: Unloaded rod
demo_steps.narration: With F = 0 the rod has its natural length L0 and cross-section A; the dashed reference coincides with the top face and ΔL = 0.

demo_steps.title: Tension (panel a)
demo_steps.narration: Equal and opposite forces pull outward on the end faces. The rod stretches: the dashed outline above the solid body marks the added length ΔL > 0 stacked on top of L0.

demo_steps.title: Compression (panel b)
demo_steps.narration: The arrows reverse and press inward. The rod shortens: the dashed ellipse now sits inside the body where the top face used to be, and the ΔL bracket measures a negative length change.

demo_steps.title: Sweep through zero
demo_steps.narration: Dragging the force from compression through zero to tension shows ΔL varying linearly with F while the radius — and therefore A — never changes.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder axis along +Y, centered on x = 0. Radius 0.55 world units (diameter 1.1), undeformed length L0 = 4.0, base at y = -2.0, top at y = +2.0. Deformation is exaggerated for legibility: ΔL = 0.8 * (F/Fmax), so |ΔL| ≤ 0.8 (20% of L0) — physically ΔL = (1/Y)(F/A)L0, strictly linear in F, with radius held constant (no Poisson narrowing shown). In tension the solid body's top face rises to y = 2.0 + ΔL and the dashed outline (dashed ellipse + two dashed vertical side lines + dashed top ellipse) occupies the band from y = 2.0 to y = 2.0 + ΔL ABOVE the body; in compression the solid top face drops to y = 2.0 - |ΔL| and a dashed ellipse is drawn INSIDE the shaded body at y = 2.0 (original face position), with the dashed side band suppressed. Arrows: thick red (#C0392B) shafts ~0.12 wide, length ~1.1, cone heads ~0.3; tension — upper arrow from y = 2.6 to 3.7 pointing up, lower arrow from y = -2.6 to -3.7 pointing down; compression — upper arrow from y = 3.7 down to the top face pointing down, lower arrow from y = -3.7 up to the base pointing up. Label 'F' (bold, arrow-over) sits beside each arrow head/tail. Brackets are thin black vertical lines with short horizontal end ticks: L0 bracket at x = -1.4 spanning the full original length (y = -2.0 to +2.0) with italic 'L0' at its midpoint; ΔL bracket in tension at x = -1.4 spanning y = 2.0 to 2.0 + ΔL with label 'ΔL'; in compression the ΔL bracket moves to the RIGHT at x = +1.4 spanning the new top face down to the dashed interior ellipse. In compression a curly leader arcs from the label 'A' (upper right, about x = 1.5, y = 3.0) to a dot on the top elliptical face. Panel caption '(a)' or '(b)' centered below at y = -4.4. Colors: cylinder body gradient #F2F2FA (left highlight) → #C9C9E4 (right shade), outline #6F6FA8, dashed lines #6F6FA8 at 55% opacity, arrows #C0392B, text/brackets near-black #1A1A1A, background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the body as a CylinderGeometry (radialSegments 64, openEnded false) whose height is rebuilt or scaled along Y each frame — scale only Y so the radius is provably constant; keep the base pinned by offsetting position.y = -2 + h/2 in tension (bottom fixed, top moves) and by moving the top face symmetrically only if desired. Apply a vertical-to-horizontal gradient with a small canvas texture or a custom shader to reproduce the flat-shaded lavender look; add an EdgesGeometry / thin tube outline for the crisp violet silhouette and separate LineLoop ellipses for the top and bottom rims. Dashed elements use LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) on an ellipse LineLoop plus two vertical segments. Arrows via ArrowHelper replacement: CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head in one Group, flipped by setting rotation.z = π for reversal. Labels (F, L0, ΔL, A, (a), (b)) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so they stay upright and crisp during orbit; the curly leader for A can be a QuadraticBezierCurve3 tube or a 2D SVG overlay. Keep lighting soft (hemisphere + weak directional) and disable strong specular to match the flat textbook shading; render with a white background and no ground plane.

authoredContext:
Tension or compression occurs when two antiparallel forces of equal magnitude act on an object along only one of its dimensions, in such a way that the object does not move. One way to envision such a situation is illustrated in the figure. A rod segment is either stretched or squeezed by a pair of forces acting along its length and perpendicular to its cross-section. The net effect of such forces is that the rod changes its length from the original length L0 that it had before the forces appeared, to a new length L that it has under the action of the forces. This change in length ΔL=L−L0 may be either elongation (when L is larger than the original length L0) or contraction (when L is smaller than the original length L0). Tensile stress and strain occur when the forces are stretching an object, causing its elongation, and the length change ΔL is positive. Compressive stress and strain occur when the forces are contracting an object, causing its shortening, and the length change ΔL is negative.

Compressive stress and strain are defined by the same formulas, the equation and the equation, respectively. The only difference from the tensile situation is that for compressive stress and strain, we take absolute values of the right-hand sides in the equation and the equation.

When an object is in either tension or compression, the net force on it is zero, but the object deforms by changing its original length L0. (a) Tension: The rod is elongated by ΔL. (b) Compression: The rod is contracted by ΔL. In both cases, the deforming force acts along the length of the rod and perpendicular to its cross-section. In the linear range of low stress, the cross-sectional area of the rod does not change.

Figure A is a schematic drawing of a cylinder with a length L0 that is under the tensile strain. Two forces at the different sides of cylinder increase its length by Delta L. Figure B is a schematic drawing of a cylinder with a length L0 that is under the compressive strain. Two forces at the different sides of cylinder reduce its length by Delta L.

discrepancies: All 3D annotation labels (F, L₀, ΔL, A, caption) render far smaller than the UI text and are essentially illegible at the default framing; in the source these are the dominant annotations (bold vector F, large italic L₀).

The dashed 'phantom' extension in panel (a) is reduced to a faint dashed ring plus two nearly-invisible side lines; the source clearly shows a dashed cylindrical segment (dashed top ellipse + dashed sides) of height ΔL above the solid body.

The ΔL bracket and its tick marks are drawn at nearly the same lateral offset as the L₀ bracket and visually collide with the top of the L₀ bracket, whereas the source separates them cleanly with a short bracket above the rod top.

The source shows both panels (a) and (b) side by side for direct comparison; the generated figure only ever shows one at a time (mitigated by a working toggle, but the side-by-side comparison of tension vs compression is lost).

The rod body is flat-shaded from a canvas gradient with no cap shading on the visible top ellipse, so the top face reads as a nearly white disc rather than the softly shaded lavender ellipse of the source.
evaluation.notes: Geometrically faithful and conceptually correct reproduction of the tension/compression rod with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (mode toggle, force slider, guided demo, clickable annotations), but the 3D labels are far too small to read and the dashed deformation outline is too faint, weakening the figure's readability as a teaching artifact.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); the issues are execution-level rendering fixes—label sizing, dashed outline visibility, bracket offsets, and shading—so the generator should refine.

interactions.label: Loading
interactions.teaches: The same rod under opposite loading: reversing the force arrows flips the sign of ΔL, so the dashed undeformed reference lies outside (stretched) or inside (shortened) the solid body.

interactions.label: Applied force F (relative)
interactions.teaches: ΔL grows in direct proportion to F while the radius stays fixed — the linear low-stress regime ΔL = (1/Y)(F/A)L0; passing through F = 0 returns the rod to its undeformed length L0.
interactions.note: Negative values are compression, positive tension; moving the slider across zero also switches the loadingMode panel labels/bracket placement.

interactions.teaches: The body is a solid cylinder of constant circular cross-section A, so the deformation is purely axial — the elliptical end faces are circles seen in perspective.

demo_steps.title: Unloaded rod
demo_steps.narration: With F = 0 the rod has its natural length L0 and cross-section A; the dashed reference coincides with the top face and ΔL = 0.

demo_steps.title: Tension (panel a)
demo_steps.narration: Equal and opposite forces pull outward on the end faces. The rod stretches: the dashed outline above the solid body marks the added length ΔL > 0 stacked on top of L0.

demo_steps.title: Compression (panel b)
demo_steps.narration: The arrows reverse and press inward. The rod shortens: the dashed ellipse now sits inside the body where the top face used to be, and the ΔL bracket measures a negative length change.

demo_steps.title: Sweep through zero
demo_steps.narration: Dragging the force from compression through zero to tension shows ΔL varying linearly with F while the radius — and therefore A — never changes.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder axis along +Y, centered on x = 0. Radius 0.55 world units (diameter 1.1), undeformed length L0 = 4.0, base at y = -2.0, top at y = +2.0. Deformation is exaggerated for legibility: ΔL = 0.8 * (F/Fmax), so |ΔL| ≤ 0.8 (20% of L0) — physically ΔL = (1/Y)(F/A)L0, strictly linear in F, with radius held constant (no Poisson narrowing shown). In tension the solid body's top face rises to y = 2.0 + ΔL and the dashed outline (dashed ellipse + two dashed vertical side lines + dashed top ellipse) occupies the band from y = 2.0 to y = 2.0 + ΔL ABOVE the body; in compression the solid top face drops to y = 2.0 - |ΔL| and a dashed ellipse is drawn INSIDE the shaded body at y = 2.0 (original face position), with the dashed side band suppressed. Arrows: thick red (#C0392B) shafts ~0.12 wide, length ~1.1, cone heads ~0.3; tension — upper arrow from y = 2.6 to 3.7 pointing up, lower arrow from y = -2.6 to -3.7 pointing down; compression — upper arrow from y = 3.7 down to the top face pointing down, lower arrow from y = -3.7 up to the base pointing up. Label 'F' (bold, arrow-over) sits beside each arrow head/tail. Brackets are thin black vertical lines with short horizontal end ticks: L0 bracket at x = -1.4 spanning the full original length (y = -2.0 to +2.0) with italic 'L0' at its midpoint; ΔL bracket in tension at x = -1.4 spanning y = 2.0 to 2.0 + ΔL with label 'ΔL'; in compression the ΔL bracket moves to the RIGHT at x = +1.4 spanning the new top face down to the dashed interior ellipse. In compression a curly leader arcs from the label 'A' (upper right, about x = 1.5, y = 3.0) to a dot on the top elliptical face. Panel caption '(a)' or '(b)' centered below at y = -4.4. Colors: cylinder body gradient #F2F2FA (left highlight) → #C9C9E4 (right shade), outline #6F6FA8, dashed lines #6F6FA8 at 55% opacity, arrows #C0392B, text/brackets near-black #1A1A1A, background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the body as a CylinderGeometry (radialSegments 64, openEnded false) whose height is rebuilt or scaled along Y each frame — scale only Y so the radius is provably constant; keep the base pinned by offsetting position.y = -2 + h/2 in tension (bottom fixed, top moves) and by moving the top face symmetrically only if desired. Apply a vertical-to-horizontal gradient with a small canvas texture or a custom shader to reproduce the flat-shaded lavender look; add an EdgesGeometry / thin tube outline for the crisp violet silhouette and separate LineLoop ellipses for the top and bottom rims. Dashed elements use LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances) on an ellipse LineLoop plus two vertical segments. Arrows via ArrowHelper replacement: CylinderGeometry shaft + ConeGeometry head in one Group, flipped by setting rotation.z = π for reversal. Labels (F, L0, ΔL, A, (a), (b)) as CSS2DRenderer/sprite HTML so they stay upright and crisp during orbit; the curly leader for A can be a QuadraticBezierCurve3 tube or a 2D SVG overlay. Keep lighting soft (hemisphere + weak directional) and disable strong specular to match the flat textbook shading; render with a white background and no ground plane.
